title: Fabrication of an acrylic microfluidic chip system
author: Nevena Milivojević Dimitrijević
materials: Use the SolidWorks 2020 CAD software package to design and build the 3D model of the chip.

steps.title: Prepare acrylic plates
steps.instruction: Cut two acrylic plates (5 mm thick) to 30 mm × 70 mm; on the bottom plate mill a cylindrical main chamber (diameter 16 mm, depth 0.8 mm) and two supply channels with a half‑cylindrical cross‑section (diameter 0.25 mm); on the top plate mill the complementary half of each supply channel and drill the two tube‑attachment holes.

substeps.instruction: Cut bottom and top plates to 30 mm × 70 mm, 5 mm thickness.
Mill bottom plate: cylindrical chamber (16 mm × 0.8 mm) and two half‑cylindrical channels (0.25 mm diameter).
Mill top plate: opposite half of each supply channel and the two tube‑attachment holes.

steps.title: Drill fitting holes
steps.instruction: Drill 3 mm diameter holes in the appropriate locations of both plates to facilitate fastening of the pipe‑fitting extensions.

steps.title: Print pipe‑fitting extensions
steps.instruction: Using a Creality CR‑10 MAX FDM printer, print the pipe‑fitting extensions from PLA filament with a layer thickness of 0.1 mm; design each fitting to attach to the end of a feed channel.

steps.title: Mill plates with CNC router
steps.instruction: Mount the acrylic plates on the homemade 3D CNC router (2.2 kW water‑cooled spindle, max 24 000 rpm, axial error 0.01 mm per 100 mm, equipped with high‑precision encoders and hybrid stepper drivers) and mill using the appropriate cutters: a 2 mm diameter blade for larger chambers/openings and a 0.25 mm ball‑end cutter for the small supply channels, setting a cutting depth of 0.25 mm to obtain the semi‑cylindrical profile.

substeps.instruction: Secure plates on CNC router bed.
Select 2 mm diameter blade for large features; mill the main chamber and any large openings.
Select 0.25 mm ball‑end cutter for supply channels; set cutting depth to 0.25 mm and mill the semi‑cylindrical channels.

steps.title: Assemble chip sandwich
steps.instruction: Attach the printed pipe‑fitting extensions to the ends of each feed channel, then align and bond the top and bottom acrylic plates to form the sandwich‑type microfluidic chip, ensuring optical transparency for microscopic monitoring.

steps.title: Connect to peristaltic pump
steps.instruction: Connect the assembled chip to a peristaltic pump via the pipe fittings to create the functional microfluidic system.
